We have carbon NMR shifts: 166.40, 144.78, 132.00, 130.07 (twice), 127.80 (twice), 52.24, 49.55, 43.55, 19.23.

Carbonyl carbons typically around 160-220 ppm. Here we have one at 166.40, which could be a carbonyl (e.g., amide, ester, acid). Others are aromatic region (~120-150). So likely only one carbonyl.

But need to be sure: 166.40 could also be a conjugated C=C (like aromatic carbon attached to hetero). However typical carbonyl for ester ~170-175, amide ~165-180, acid ~180-185, ketone ~200-210. So 166.40 fits carbonyl.

Thus answer integer 1.

We could also check IR for C=O stretch. Let's quickly get IR to confirm.
